Title: Malaysia women-only trains gain global attention after French documentary feature
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's public rail network has captured international attention after being featured in the French travel documentary series Des trains pas comme les autres (Amazing Train Journeys).
In a video clip that went viral online, the documentary showcased Kuala Lumpur's designated women-only coaches, drawing praise from local commuters and international viewers.
"In the Kuala Lumpur metro in Malaysia, certain carriages are reserved exclusively for women. Marked by pink stripes, they offer a space where women can travel with greater peace of mind," the official episode description read.
Malaysian netizens took to social media platforms to express their support for the initiative, highlighting how the designated coaches enhance daily commutes.
On Threads, user @cik.kentangbatu shared that the women-only carriages were practical for peak-hour travel.
"The women's coach is so practical when commuting to work. Even if we have to squeeze against other women, it doesn't matter. I feel safe, and women support one another even if they are complete strangers," she wrote.
Another user, @damien_mikeng, said the initiative reflected Malaysia's cultural values.
"Culturally, Malaysians of all races and religions naturally observe personal boundaries between genders," he posted.
Echoing similar sentiments, user @fauzanizam succinctly added that the initiative fundamentally boiled down to "providing comfort and safety".
[[nid:1496781]]
The documentary feature also sparked a broader global conversation on Facebook, with international viewers pointing out that women-only public transport initiatives exist worldwide as a practical courtesy.
Facebook user Martine Carlier noted: "In Mexico, there have been pink buses reserved for women and their children for years."
Meanwhile, another commenter, Olivier Noirot-Cosson, said such measures transcended culture and religion.
"Nothing extraordinary, and nothing to do with religion. When I went to England in the 1970s, there were 'women only' compartments. It is simply about respect and comfort," he shared.
Women-only coaches were first introduced on Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd's trains in 2010, before being expanded to the MRT Kajang Line and MRT Putrajaya Line by Prasarana Malaysia Bhd to provide a safer and more comfortable travel experience for female passengers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'No need to come to Negri': Zahid tells Sanusi to focus on Kedah, avoid divisive rhetoric
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has cautioned Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor not to stir up racial and religious sensitivities in Negri Sembilan ahead of its state election.
Zahid said the Kedah menteri besar should stay in Kedah for the remainder of the campaign period and focus on governing his state instead of campaigning in Negri Sembilan.
"We still have six more days of campaigning. It would be better for him to keep himself busy governing Kedah," Zahid said after attending the Salam Agrikomoditi Madani programme at Dataran Melang.
"I don't think there is any need for him to come to Negri Sembilan. Let us manage Negri Sembilan in our own way."
Zahid added that he did not intend to advise Sanusi, but merely remind him to watch his words.
"Even if there is a tiger in his heart, when he speaks, let only the goat come out," he said.
"I do not want any interpretation that could end up causing unease among various groups in society.
"If his intention is to show unity among the ummah, there is no need to touch on issues involving ethnicity, religion, culture or the background of other races in this country."
Zahid's remarks came after a news portal reported that Sanusi, during a ceramah in Jempol, said Malays had no other homeland, while Indians, Chinese, Cambodians, and Thais each had countries associated with their ethnic groups.
Zahid said that Malaysia's diversity was part of its natural social fabric and should not be exploited for political gain.
"I have confidence in the country's plural society. This diversity is sunnatullah (God's ordained order).
"There is no need to raise such matters. If they truly want to build friendships, then do so properly, not by bringing up other issues," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar rejects Sanusi's 'Tanah Melayu' remarks, says Malaysia must embrace all citizens
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has rejected Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's remarks on Tanah Melayu, saying Malaysia's strength lies in embracing all citizens.
Anwar said Malaysia, independent for nearly 70 years, should not have leaders making statements that could insult or exclude other communities.
He said while Malays were historically associated with Tanah Melayu, Malaysia's citizens came from diverse ancestral backgrounds and all who accepted the Constitution and contributed to the country must be regarded as part of the nation.
"Malays, the majority of whom originated from Tanah Melayu, also include those with roots from Indonesia. There are also those of Chinese and Korean descent, and we cannot reject them as not being rakyat," he said.
He was responding to remarks by Sanusi during the Perikatan Nasional (PN) campaign for the Negri Sembilan state election, where the coalition used racial and religious rhetoric, including suggesting that different ethnic groups in Malaysia could fall back on ancestral homelands outside the country.
On Thursday, Sanusi, who is also PN election director, said Tanah Melayu was the only homeland for Malays, unlike other ethnic groups who, he claimed, could return to countries such as India, China or Thailand.
He also claimed Malay political power and economic control were increasingly being eroded and could disappear within 10 years without drastic changes.
Anwar said such views were unacceptable, stressing that Malaysians from all communities who uphold the Federal Constitution and contribute to the nation must be embraced.
"Especially among the Chinese and Indian communities, who are loyal, accept the Constitution and are good citizens, we must embrace them as Malaysia's strength," he said after the launch of SMKA Sheikh Tahir Jalaluddin here today.
"I do not agree at all with any perception that insults or sidelines the role of any community in our country," he added.
Anwar said Malaysia's diversity should be viewed as a source of strength rather than a basis for division.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke urges NS election rivals to campaign positively, avoid arrogance
Article:
JELEBU: All parties contesting the Negri Sembilan election should campaign positively and avoid arrogant statements
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the ultimate decision on the fate of any candidate or party rested entirely with the voters.
"There is no need for us, as cabinet partners, to be arrogant. We should campaign positively.
"Whether someone gets defeated or not is up to the people, because the voters are the ones who will decide.
"The local people know better than Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid. If he says there has been no development, the Chennah state constituency is also under the Jelebu parliamentary constituency.
"So who holds the Jelebu parliamentary seat? There's no need to be arrogant," he told reporters after a walkabout at the Titi morning market today.
Yesterday, Zahid said that if BN wins the Chennah and Linggi state seats in this election, it would succeed in wresting control of Negri Sembilan from Pakatan Harapan.
He said the objective centres on the Chennah and Linggi state constituencies, where Loke and Negri Sembilan PH chairman Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun are contesting, respectively.
Commenting on facilities in Chennah, Loke said the rural constituency has received various improvements and infrastructure upgrades for the benefit and comfort of residents.
He said development in the area is a shared responsibility since Chennah falls under the administration of the Jelebu parliamentary constituency.
"The people know better, and I will continue to remain positive and campaign positively. We will continue appealing to voters to support PH so that we can keep serving them.
"The voters here know me, and I will continue engaging with people from all communities — Malay, Chinese, Indian, as well as the Orang Asli," he said.
Loke also rejected claims by some parties and media analyses suggesting that the combined vote share of BN and Perikatan Nasional in the 15th General Election reached 58 per cent in Chennah.
"That's not accurate. Since becoming the elected representative here, I have consistently received more than 50 per cent of the vote since 2013. So some of those figures are actually incorrect," he said.
On the increasingly intense second week of campaigning, with Chennah being labelled one of the election's "hot seats," Loke said such a situation is normal in any election.
"Yes, every seat is a hot seat. Which election isn't competitive? We will campaign calmly and continue to stay calm.
"The response to PH has been quite good so far. We are using different approaches depending on the area, including holding meetings in villages. With one week of campaigning remaining, we will continue to build on this positive momentum," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China evacuates 20,000 people as Typhoon Noul nears
Article:
BEIJING: Authorities have evacuated more than 20,000 people and suspended railway services in southern China as Typhoon Noul approaches, threatening torrential rain and gale-force winds, according to state media.
The typhoon is forecast to make landfall along the coastal area stretching from Hong Kong to Guangdong province between Saturday evening and Sunday morning, China's National Meteorological Center said.
It maintained an orange typhoon alert on Saturday, the second-highest level in its four-tier warning system, after warning that parts of Guangdong and neighbouring Fujian province would experience gales and torrential rain.
More than 20,000 people had been evacuated in Guangdong, state broadcaster CCTV said in a bulletin late on Friday.
Fishing vessels operating at sea in the province had returned to port to shelter from the storm, it added.
Guangdong will suspend some train services on Saturday morning, with all rail services in the province to be halted on Sunday, CCTV said.
Schools in Guangdong's Chaozhou city were instructed to suspend on-campus activities, according to local media reports.
Extreme weather has already wreaked havoc on southern and central China this month, with 39 people killed when Typhoon Maysak triggered devastating floods in Guangxi.
Maysak also caused thunderstorms and gale-force winds that killed 11 people and injured 331 in the central province of Hubei.
Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of extreme weather events worldwide will increase as the planet continues to warm because of fossil fuel emissions.
China is the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gases, but it is also a global renewable energy powerhouse that aims to make its massive economy carbon neutral by 2060.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt absorbs higher oil costs to keep RON95 at RM1.99, says Anwar
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH: Malaysia is maintaining the RON95 petrol price at RM1.99 despite rising global oil prices by spending up to RM50 billion a year on fuel subsidies, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar said the government continued to shield consumers from higher fuel costs by absorbing billions of ringgit in subsidies, even as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East pushed up crude oil prices and import costs.
"Alhamdulillah, despite all these challenges, Malaysia is still able to maintain the RON95 price at RM1.99 and diesel at RM2.10.
"But the government has to pay for it. It is not free. People think RM1.99 is the actual market price, but it is not. The government bears the difference," he said when closing National Training Week 2026 here today.
Anwar said crude oil prices, which were projected at about US$70 per barrel when the government prepared the Budget, had since climbed to between US$80 and US$85 per barrel and, at one point, reached US$100 following the conflict involving Iran and disruptions affecting the Strait of Hormuz.
Although Petronas produced part of the country's fuel supply, Malaysia still imported about half of its petroleum requirements, leaving it exposed to higher global prices.
Anwar said Putrajaya was expected to spend between RM40 billion and RM50 billion annually on fuel subsidies to keep pump prices low.
This was in addition to RM15 billion to RM16 billion allocated for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah programmes, as well as RM18 billion a year for civil service salary increases.
"These measures underscore the government's commitment to protecting Malaysians from rising living costs while maintaining fiscal discipline and implementing economic reforms," he added.
Anwar said he was not complaining but merely wanted people to understand.
"This money comes from government revenue and taxes," he said.
Despite the mounting fiscal commitments, Anwar said the government would continue to balance sound public finances with measures to ease the cost of living while pursuing reforms to strengthen Malaysia's economy.
He said the country's economic fundamentals remained strong, citing a stronger ringgit, record investment inflows and one of the highest growth rates in Asia as evidence that the government's reform agenda was delivering results.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man arrested over seditious, insulting Facebook post against Islam
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police have arrested a man for allegedly uploading a Facebook post containing seditious and insulting remarks against Islam.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said a report was lodged at 12.38am yesterday after a member of the public spotted the viral post on social media.
"Checks showed that the owner of a Facebook account under the name 'Fadzil Zahari' shared several screenshots believed to have been uploaded by account owner 'Parthiban Ragu', which contained statements insulting Islam as well as offensive and obscene expressions directed at Allah SWT and Prophet Muhammad SAW.
"Acting on information, a team of officers arrested a 37-year-old man at 1am today in Iskandar Puteri," he said in a statement.
He said checks revealed the suspect had no prior criminal record, adding that police seized two mobile phones to assist in the investigation.
The suspect was brought to the Johor Baru magistrate's court, where a four-day remand order was granted until Tuesday.
The case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 298 of the Penal Code.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khaled: Expulsion of Israelis in line with Malaysia's longstanding policy
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Malaysia's decision to expel Israeli citizens aligns with its longstanding policy of not recognising Israel.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Malaysia remained firm in its stance, and that enforcement action taken was in line with this policy.
"What happened with the expulsion was to ensure no Israeli nationals were involved in the Network School.
"Our policy has always been clear. We do not allow Israelis to enter the country," he told reporters after opening the Pasir Gudang Umno division delegates meeting here today.
Khaled was responding to queries on the expulsion and calls by members of the United States Congress to halt funding for the International Military Education and Training (IMET) programme for Malaysia.
He said Malaysia's firm implementation of the policy had not affected funding under the IMET programme.
"Our policy is simply that we do not recognise the State of Israel. If members of Congress want to make such demands, that is a matter between them and their government," he said.
Recently, eight members of the US Congress urged their administration to review security and economic ties with Malaysia following action taken against an Israeli national who allegedly entered the country using a second country's passport.
In a letter to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio dated July 21, the lawmakers also urged Washington to consider suspending IMET funding if Malaysia did not alter its position within 15 days.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has said the government would not compromise and would expel any Israeli national found in Malaysia.
He added that all security agencies were conducting a thorough investigation into allegations that Israeli nationals had entered the country in connection with the Network School issue in Forest City.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia one step closer to achieving high-income nation, says Ramanan
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH: Malaysia is one step closer to achieving high-income status after recording its highest Gross National Income (GNI) and economic output, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said.
Speaking at the National Training Week (NTW) 2026 closing ceremony officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim here today, Ramanan said the latest World Bank data for 2025 showed Malaysia had made significant progress.
He said Malaysia's GNI per capita, based on the World Bank's Atlas method, had reached US$12,380 — the highest since independence — while the country's economy expanded to a record GDP of US$472 billion.
"For the 2027 financial year, the World Bank's high-income threshold is a GNI per capita of US$14,000. Malaysia is now only one step away from achieving that status.
"We are not far from our goal," he said.
Ramanan attributed the achievement to Anwar's leadership, saying the country had been placed back on the right economic trajectory over the past four years.
He also highlighted Malaysia's success in attracting its second-highest level of foreign investment in history in 2025, citing the World Investment Report 2026, while noting that the economy grew 5.8 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, among the strongest performances in Asean.
Ramanan said strong macroeconomic performance alone was insufficient unless it translated into broader prosperity for Malaysians.
"These impressive economic figures will mean little if the opportunities and wealth created benefit only those who are already well-off while others remain spectators," he added.
He said initiatives such as NTW were crucial to ensuring Malaysians had opportunities to upskill and reskill, enabling them to secure better jobs and improve their incomes.
Ramanan said the Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) played a key role in strengthening the country's talent development ecosystem by ensuring employers' levy contributions were channelled towards meaningful workforce training.
In Penang alone, he said, more than 4,000 employers were registered with HRD Corp, covering over 445,000 workers, while RM129.72 million in training levies had been collected in the first half of this year.
Of that amount, RM113 million had been disbursed to support workforce training and skills development in the state.
Ramanan said the ministry remained committed to strengthening governance to ensure every sen collected through the levy was used responsibly to benefit Malaysian workers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Houthis claim strike on Saudi Arabia as conflict deepens
Article:
SANAA: Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia on Saturday, hours after vowing to retaliate against the kingdom for attacks as the Middle East war expanded.
Riyadh struck Houthi military targets in Hodeidah on Friday, with rebel media reporting two people wounded after the Yemeni group announced a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and attacked its ships.
The flare-up marks a new front in the war that has engulfed the region following US-Israeli strikes on Teheran in February, and comes on top of Iran's parallel blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh's only other maritime route.
The rebels accused Saudi Arabia of a "dangerous escalation" and said its actions "will not go unanswered".
The Houthis' Ansarollah media said on Telegram early on Saturday that a "Yemeni missile strike" had sparked fires in the southern Saudi city of Jizan on the Red Sea.
Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the claim.
But Riyadh's civil defence agency issued brief warnings to residents in Jizan and Yanbu early on Saturday of "potential danger", only to lift the warnings minutes later.
Similar warnings have been issued in the past when missiles or drones were fired at the kingdom.
The warning came after the Saudi-led coalition said on Friday it had hit Houthi sites and destroyed targets threatening commercial vessels in response to attacks on Red Sea shipping.
A Yemeni security source told AFP that a naval base in the port city of Hodeidah and a military camp on Kamaran Island were among the Saudi targets.
The Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi ships earlier this week, with Saudi Arabia confirming one of the attacks in the Red Sea.
BLOCKADE
The Yemeni security source, who requested anonymity, said the Saudi strikes targeted a telecommunications building near Hodeidah's port and a naval base at Ras al-Kathib in Hodeidah.
The Houthis' Al Masirah television channel said two people were wounded — a worker in Hodeidah and a woman on Kamaran Island.
It said a telecommunications building had been hit in Hodeidah.
On Monday, the rebels warned in a radio message to ships that they would target vessels "belonging to (the) Saudi enemy" that did not comply with their blockade.
Saudi state media quoted a transport authority official on Friday as saying "the vessel (NCC MASA), belonging to a Saudi company, was targeted while sailing in the Red Sea today... resulting in minor damage to the vessel's hull".
The ship resumed its course, the Saudi Press Agency (SPA) added.
Red Sea access has become vital for Saudi Arabia to keep shipping oil as traffic in the Strait of Hormuz is disrupted.
In April and May, all of Saudi Arabia's seaborne crude exports departed from its Red Sea port of Yanbu, according to Kpler data. It represented 92 per cent of all seaborne crude exports in June and 78 per cent so far in July.
The Houthis have been at war with Yemen's government since 2014, in a conflict that has killed hundreds of thousands of people.
The recent exchange of fire threatens a 2022 truce that has held despite expiring.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bentong crash: Car went out of control on hilly, winding stretch
Article:
BENTONG: The accident which claimed the lives of six friends on the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Highway near Kampung Jambu Rias here early today occurred after their car went out of control on a hilly, winding stretch.
The car then collided with an oncoming lorry, leaving the six occupants dead and the lorry driver seriously injured.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the car was travelling from Kuantan towards Kuala Lumpur when it went out of control while negotiating a bend on the hilly stretch.
"The car is believed to have lost control and veered to the right side of the road.
"It then collided with the oncoming lorry, killing the driver and five passengers at the scene.
"The lorry driver was injured and rushed to Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (HoSHAS) in Temerloh for treatment," he said in a statement.
The deceased were identified as V. Mugilan, 25; K. Dineshvaran, 22; K. Alaganathan, 21; A. Kanabati Raja, 19; K. Sasi Kumar, 17; and M. Paranthaman, 16.
Azry said all six bodies were sent to HoSHAS for post-mortem.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Formula 1 announcement to be made on Sunday
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Malaysia's potential return to the Formula 1 calendar will be announced tomorrow, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said, amid uncertainty over races in the Middle East.
Anwar, however, did not disclose details of the government's plans when asked about reports that Formula 1 could return to the Sepang International Circuit.
"F1, we will announce on Sunday," he told reporters.
He was speaking after officiating the launch of SMKA Sheikh Tahir Jalaluddin here today.
Reports have emerged that Sepang could be considered as a replacement venue should the championship face disruptions to its 2026 calendar due to escalating tensions in the Middle East.
The Race, a motorsport news outlet, reported that Sepang had become a potential option for Formula 1 organisers seeking to protect the season schedule if races in the region were cancelled.
Malaysia hosted Formula 1 races at Sepang from 1999 to 2017, with the circuit becoming one of the sport's best-known venues in Asia before the country withdrew from the calendar due to rising hosting costs and declining ticket sales.
A return would mark Malaysia's comeback to the
Formula 1 calendar
and could revive Sepang's position as an international motorsport destination.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump jokes about another term at rescheduled correspondents' dinner
Article:
HAMILTON: US President Donald Trump joked about running for another term late on Friday as he donned a "Trump 2028" hat during the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA) annual dinner, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.
"I'm pleased to announce my intention to run for a fourth term as president of the United States," said Trump, before joking that he had "won three times" and was "getting very good at running for president".
His remarks appeared to be a joke about seeking another term in office, which would conflict with the US Constitution's 22nd Amendment, which limits presidents to two elected terms.
The president also mocked the media, saying he believed some journalists "don't like" him and claimed that he receives "93 per cent negative publicity".
"But this place is really the largest group of Trump derangement syndrome people ever put together at one time," he said.
The dinner was rescheduled after the original event in April was interrupted by a shooting near a security checkpoint while Trump administration officials were attending the gathering.
Outgoing WHCA president Weijia Jiang opened the rescheduled event by vowing that journalists would not be intimidated by violence.
"We are back, we will not be intimidated, we refuse to let an act of violence have the final word," said Jiang.
Referring to the shooting during his remarks, Trump said that "a tremendous amount was learned about security and about other things, the dangers of what we all do".
He joked that the rescheduled dinner was better than the original, saying: "Just like my presidency, the second time is always better."
Trump also addressed Iran, claiming that the US military had destroyed "250 jets" and "159 boats" belonging to Iran.
"They have very few drones left, despite what you see," he said, adding that Iran was speaking with the US and wanted to reach a deal.
"I don't think they're ready to. I don't think it's time yet. But I'm willing to listen, but they cannot have a nuclear weapon," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johari: Voters to decide BN manifesto appeal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Voters in Negri Sembilan will ultimately decide whether Barisan Nasional's election manifesto is convincing enough to win their support, Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said.
Johari, the Investment, Trade and Industry Minister, said every coalition would present its own commitments, but the final judgment rested with the electorate.
"People in Negri Sembilan can evaluate it themselves because every party will come out with its own manifesto.
"In the end, the victory of any party depends on how the people assess each party, their commitments, and what they have done before and after," he told reporters after attending the National Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia 50th Annual General Meeting 2026.
Johari said voters would assess not only the promises made by political parties, but also their credibility, track record and ability to deliver on their commitments.
When asked whether BN could expect stronger support from Chinese voters, Johari avoided speculation.
"You have to ask DAP, MCA and Gerakan," he said.
His remarks came after BN launched its manifesto for the
Negri Sembilan election
, themed "Hebatkan Semula Negri Sembilan: Kestabilan Dibina, Negeri Dijaga, Rakyat Dibela, Kemakmuran Dicipta", which outlines nine key thrusts, 88 action plans and 15 initiatives under the Salam Sejahtera Scheme.
BN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan yesterday said
the manifesto
was not a "delayed plan", but a continuation of development agendas that had been stalled following BN's defeat in the state in 2018.
Mohamad said several high-impact projects planned under the previous BN administration were disrupted following the change in government, with some projects later deviating from their original objectives.
Mohamad, who is also Negri Sembilan BN chairman, dismissed claims that BN's manifesto had received input from Perikatan Nasional (PN), following PN information chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa's remarks on the possibility of merging both coalitions' manifestos.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johari: Malaysia gets two years to amend laws under US trade pact
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will have up to two years to amend its laws to address concerns over forced labour and excess industrial capacity once the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (ART) with the United States is ratified.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the timeline was part of Malaysia's commitments under the agreement, allowing Putrajaya to introduce or amend legislation to address regulatory gaps identified by the US.
"They are giving us two years to amend the laws. It is not something that has to be done immediately.
"Once we ratify the agreement, we will have two years to rectify the laws that we currently do not have," he told reporters after attending the National Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia (NCCIM) 50th Annual General Meeting (AGM) 2026.
Johari said the Human Resources Ministry had been informed of the required changes and was aware of the legal provisions that needed to be amended or introduced.
"The Human Resources Ministry has already been informed, and they know which sections need to be amended and what new laws need to be introduced.
"They will proceed once we finalise the ART."
He said Malaysia already had comprehensive domestic laws to address forced labour, including provisions against the employment of undocumented foreign workers and requirements for employers to provide proper accommodation.
However, he said the legal gap involved products made using forced labour overseas that entered Malaysia through global supply chains.
"We already have laws to protect workers in Malaysia. The issue is that we do not yet have laws to prevent products made using forced labour in third countries from entering Malaysia as inputs, being processed here and then exported as Malaysian products."
Johari said this was among the issues that led to Malaysia being subjected to a 10 per cent tariff under the US Section 301 investigation on forced labour.
He said Malaysia was among 66 economies investigated by the US but only faced scrutiny under two categories — forced labour and excess capacity.
"The 10 per cent relates to forced labour. We still do not know what rate, if any, will be imposed under the excess capacity investigation.
"Once that is determined, it will be combined to form Malaysia's overall rate."
Johari said the new legal framework would help ensure Malaysia's exports were not affected by raw materials sourced from supply chains linked to forced labour.
"If we use raw materials produced through forced labour to manufacture our own products, that could affect our exports."
He added that Malaysia had previously taken enforcement action against companies linked to forced labour allegations, including cases involving plantation firms whose exports were restricted until improvements were made.
On excess industrial capacity, Johari said further legislative amendments would also be required to address concerns raised by the US.
"Excess capacity also requires legal reforms. That is why the agreement provides a two-year implementation period."
He said Malaysia remained committed to aligning its trade and labour practices with international standards as part of its obligations under the ART.
Earlier, US President Donald Trump's administration announced plans to impose new tariffs of 10 per cent and 12.5 per cent on goods from 60 trading partners, including Malaysia, effective July 24.
The measure comes amid allegations that affected nations failed to enforce forced labour bans, coinciding with the expiration of a temporary 10 per cent global tariff.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Two men held after police chase involving Nissan Grand Livina
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Two men in their 50s with extensive criminal and drug-related records were arrested after a car chase from Sri Damansara to Gombak late last night.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said the incident began at about 11.57pm when the driver of a Nissan Grand Livina allegedly sped away from a police inspection at Persiaran Dagang, Sri Damansara.
He said the vehicle was driven dangerously through several roads before it was located at Jalan Sungai Pusu in Gombak.
"When police attempted to make an arrest, the suspect acted aggressively by reversing the vehicle into a police patrol car before fleeing again.
"The vehicle also crashed into two cars parked by the roadside," he said in a statement today.
Shamsudin said police subsequently arrested the driver and his passenger, both men in their 50s, to assist with investigations.
"Checks found that the first suspect had 23 drug-related offences.
"The second suspect had eight drug-related offences and 10 previous offences," he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of his duties and Section 279 of the same Act for reckless driving.
He said investigations revealed that both suspects were friends.
"Urine tests will be conducted on both suspects to facilitate further investigations," he said.
Police have urged witnesses with information to contact the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters operations room at 03-7966 2222.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Suspect remanded over Klang cash van robbery bid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The suspect arrested over the attempted robbery of a cash-in-transit security van outside a bank in Bukit Tinggi, Klang, earlier this week has been remanded for six days to assist in investigations.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the remand order took effect yesterday and will remain in force until July 29.
"The suspect has been remanded for six days until July 29. Initial investigations found that he acted alone in the incident," he said when contacted today.
On Monday, the suspect allegedly
attempted
to rob a security van carrying cash outside a bank in Bukit Tinggi, Klang.
The attempt was foiled after security personnel resisted the attack, forcing the suspect to flee the scene.
However, he
escaped

Title: Malaysia strongly condemns mass incursion into Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has strongly condemned the mass incursion into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound by more than 4,200 Israeli settlers and far-right extremists.
The Foreign Ministry said the deliberate and provocative act of storming Islam's third holiest site on Thursday was conducted under the protection of Israeli occupying forces and included an Israeli cabinet minister.
It said the incident, accompanied by restrictions on Palestinian worshippers and unauthorised religious activities within the compound, constitutes a blatant violation of the historical and legal status quo governing the holy site.
"Such actions also represent a grave breach of international law and relevant United Nations resolutions concerning the status of Occupied East Jerusalem.
"Malaysia views this reckless provocation as part of a continued pattern of violations and escalatory actions by the Israeli regime in Occupied East Jerusalem aimed at undermining the sanctity of the holy site and altering its historical, legal, and demographic character," the ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, said in a statement today.
Wisma Putra said the actions disregard the religious sensitivities of Muslims worldwide and called on the international community, particularly the UN Security Council, to take urgent action to stop violations and threats to regional peace and stability.
"The sanctity of Islamic holy sites must be respected and preserved, and the rights of Muslim worshippers to access and perform religious obligations at the holy site must be guaranteed," Wisma Putra said.
Malaysia also reaffirmed its unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people and its steadfast support for their inalienable rights, including self-determination and the establishment of an independent, sovereign Palestinian state based on pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police propose merit system for students reporting bullying, extortion, and drugs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have proposed introducing a merit system for students who report bullying, extortion, or drug involvement in schools.
Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said the proposal was among measures put forward to strengthen crime prevention following several violent attacks involving students.
He said the system would help schools detect misconduct early and cultivate a culture of reporting.
"A merit system is proposed for students who provide information on bullying, extortion, or drugs to encourage a reporting culture. Expanding closed-circuit television (CCTV) coverage to all schools is also proposed to assist wardens and teachers in monitoring students," he said.
The proposal follows several alarming incidents, including the fatal stabbing of a 16-year-old female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, on Oct 14 last year. A 14-year-old male student was subsequently charged with murder in connection with the incident in the school's toilet.
On July 6, a 15-year-old Form Three female student was injured after being stabbed by a classmate at a secondary school in Banting. The victim suffered injuries to several parts of her body, including her lungs, while the suspect was charged with attempted murder.
Days later, a 13-year-old Form One male student allegedly pointed a penknife at a schoolmate and chased him for about 50 metres at a secondary school in Alor Gajah, Melaka. A teacher persuaded the student to hand over the knife, and no injuries were reported.
Noor Hisam said physical and emotional bullying in schools remained a serious concern due to its long-term impact on student safety and mental well-being.
He also called for specialised training for school security guards to recognise early warning signs, alongside empowering Crime Prevention Clubs and school cadet units.
On the role of School Liaison Officers (PPS), Noor Hisam said police officers have been assigned to all 10,255 schools under the Education Ministry, comprising 2,481 secondary schools and 7,774 primary schools.
"Each PPS is required to visit their assigned school at least once a month," he said, adding that officers meet with student affairs and discipline teachers to identify at-risk behaviour early.
He said officers also collaborate with school counsellors to address cases up to the family level, conduct briefings during assemblies on bullying, fights, and traffic safety, attend Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) meetings, and conduct spot checks on bags and classrooms alongside teachers.
Police mobile patrol vehicles and Motorcycle Patrol Units also conduct patrols around schools during operating hours, with night patrols conducted at boarding schools.
"This structure allows two-way communication between schools and the police. The PPS does not merely react after an incident occurs," he said.
He added that while the PPS mechanism remains relevant and effective, its success depends on the commitment of school administrators, teachers, parents, and the community in providing early information.
"Legal action will also be taken against students confirmed to be involved in crime or drugs, in line with the existing role of the PPS," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nail-free for nearly a century, Durah's heritage home stands the test of time
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Amid the timeless beauty of the traditional village of Seri Menanti, which continues to preserve the heritage of Adat Perpatih, stands a nearly century-old rumah limas, showcasing the refinement of Malay architecture that has withstood the test of time.
Nestled among modern homes, the house, built around 1927, has retained its original appearance, bearing witness to the journey from the era of kerosene lamps and red dirt roads to today's fast-changing world.
Even more remarkably, the house, which stands on 12 pillars, was built without the use of a single iron nail.
Instead, craftsmen of the past joined every timber component using the traditional pasak (wooden pegs) and tanggam (mortise-and-tenon) technique, a woodworking skill that has enabled the house to remain sturdy across generations.
At 84, Durah Bidin, affectionately known as Wan, continues to live in the ancestral home inherited from her maternal grandmother.
"This was originally my grandmother's house. It has been here for as long as I can remember, and I grew up here," she told Bernama recently.
A native of Seri Menanti from the Tanah Datar clan, she spent her childhood in the house, with almost every chapter of her life beginning and unfolding beneath the same roof.
"This house is more than just a shelter. It is a place filled with family memories, where I grew up with my mother and relatives," she said.
Stepping into the house, located within the Seri Menanti state constituency, is like taking a journey back in time.
Its sturdy wooden floor, walls that have deepened in colour with age, and solid pillars stand as silent witnesses to the generations that once lived there, each leaving behind stories and cherished memories.
According to Durah, most of the house was built using punak timber, which remains in excellent condition to this day, while the original kitchen was constructed with  tembusu wood, reflecting the wisdom of earlier generations in selecting durable building materials.
"Punak wood is very strong, much like teak. That's why the house is still standing today and remains perfectly livable," she said.
The unique architectural design and remarkable durability of the heritage house have made it a regular destination for architecture students and researchers studying its structure and construction techniques.
"Many architecture students come here. They study old houses, measure the pillars and examine every detail," she said.
Durah hopes her family's rumah limas will continue to be preserved so that future generations can appreciate and understand the elegance of traditional Malay architecture with Minangkabau influences, a defining feature of Negeri Sembilan's identity. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Prayer gathering ends in tragedy for crash victim [WATCH]
Article:
TEMERLOH: One of the six victims of a pre-dawn crash in Bentong this morning had gone to attend a prayer ceremony with his family before heading out with friends, unaware it would be his final night.
Mugilan Vraputiran, 25, was killed when the car he was travelling in collided with a one-tonne lorry on Jalan Karak Lama near the Jambu Rias Health Clinic at about 4.25am today.
His sister, Moganah Vraputiran, 33, said Mugilan later went out with several friends after the ceremony in Sungai Kawang, including one who had recently returned from Singapore after a long absence.
"After prayers, they went out to eat and catch up. We did not know where they went after that.
"I never expected that to be our last meeting. He was his usual cheerful self and showed no signs of anything being wrong," she said when met.
Mugilan was among six men aged between 15 and 25 killed in the crash. The other victims were Dinesvaran Kumar, 21; Alaganathan Krishnan, 20; Kanabati Raja Arunasalam, 18; Kiisyen Sasi Kumar, 16; and Paranthaman Marutayah, 15.
Mugilan, the youngest of four siblings and the family's only son, also leaves behind a two-year-old child.
"He was a good person, close to the family and always helped our mother. His loss is a huge blow to us.
"What makes it even more heartbreaking is that he leaves behind a two-year-old child. We still cannot believe he is gone," she said.
Mugilan's remains will be buried in Mentakab after the post-mortem is completed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Mizan in good health, to undergo follow-up treatment abroad
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, is in good health and will undergo scheduled follow-up treatment abroad under the care of his medical team.
The Office of the Sultan of Terengganu, in a statement released through the Information Department today, said Sultan Mizan expressed his appreciation to the people for their continued prayers for his well-being.
"May Allah continue to bless His Royal Highness the Sultan with good and lasting health, and ease all of his affairs," the statement read.

Title: Teenage student arrested after newborn's body found at university hostel
Article:
KUALA LANGAT: A teenage student has been arrested after the body of a newborn baby wrapped in cloth was found in a university hostel rubbish disposal area here yesterday.
District police chief Superintendent Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi said police received a report at 12.20pm from a man who discovered the infant's body at the hostel block's rubbish collection point.
"Following investigations, police identified and arrested a teenage female student believed to be connected to the case to assist in investigations," he said in a statement today.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 318 of the Penal Code for concealing birth by secret disposal of a dead body, an offence that carries up to two years' imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.S
Those with information can contact the nearest police station or the Kuala Langat district police headquarters operations room at 03-3187 2222.

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar urges youths to reject divisive narratives, engage with government
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has assured young Malaysians that the government is listening to their concerns while urging them to reject divisive ideologies.
Anwar said the Madani government welcomed criticism and suggestions from young people, stressing that their feedback was essential to improving government programmes and ensuring no one was left behind.
"Do not be influenced by ideologies that weaken and destroy.
"Work together to build a stronger, more prosperous nation. Malaysia could only achieve developed nation status if its youths refused to be swayed by narratives that sowed hatred and division among communities.
"Young people must rise as a giant force to bring change and uplift the dignity of all Malaysians. Work together, work hard, improve ourselves and make Malaysia a great and successful country," he said when closing the National Training Week (NTW) 2026 here today.
Anwar said every Malaysian, regardless of race or background, deserved equal opportunities to succeed, stressing that the government's focus was to uplift all communities instead of pitting them against one another.
He acknowledged that the government did not have immediate solutions to every issue but said it was committed to making progress through collaboration.
"I am not here to say we have all the answers. I am not here to say we can solve everything overnight.
"But I am here to say we can make a start, and we have the humility to say, 'Yes, we can do better, and we can do better when we work together'," he added.
Anwar urged the young people to give their views, their criticisms and their suggestions.
"If there are gaps, weaknesses or groups that have been left behind, tell us, and we will improve," he said, noting that the government's role was to continuously listen, refine its policies and expand opportunities for all Malaysians, particularly the younger generation, through initiatives such as NTW.
He also urged youths to channel their energy towards acquiring new skills, constructive engagement and nation-building instead of being distracted by narratives that sow hatred and division.
Meanwhile, Anwar called on the participants present at the NTW to take advantage of the training opportunities offered and engage directly with officials from the Human Resources Ministry, the Human Resource Development Corporation and the minister.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Cabinet likely to approve Tabung Haji RCI report release, says Anwar
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH: The Cabinet is expected to decide this Wednesday on whether to publicly release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji, says Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The prime minister said he had no objections to making the report public and would table the matter at the Cabinet meeting next week.
"I have no objection. I agree. But we must follow the process. When I bring it to the Cabinet on Wednesday, I believe the Cabinet will agree," he said at the closing ceremony of National Training Week 2026 today.
"I have no objection. I agree. But we must follow the process. When I bring it to the Cabinet on Wednesday, I believe the Cabinet will agree," he said at the closing ceremony of National Training Week 2026 today.
Anwar said the report's release had been deferred previously after Tabung Haji requested more time to implement reforms under its new management.
"Previously, we agreed to delay the report because Tabung Haji said it needed time to make improvements.
"There is now a new management team to put things right, and we are ready for it to be made public," he added.
Anwar said the government had opted against releasing the report earlier to avoid undermining public confidence in the pilgrimage fund while the reforms were being implemented.
"If it had been released too early, people might have
lost confidence
in Tabung Haji. Tabung Haji today is different," he stressed.
Highlighting the institution's turnaround, Anwar said Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Salman had recently congratulated him after Tabung Haji was recognised as having the best management among haj organisations worldwide.
He said the recognition underscored the government's efforts to strengthen governance and restore confidence in public institutions.
"When we do our work properly and correct past excesses, we can restore our dignity and elevate our institutions," he said.

Title: Crisis-hit Flavio Bolsonaro launches presidential candidacy in Brazil
Article:
SAO PAULO: Battered by a string of political crises, Flavio Bolsonaro will formally launch his candidacy for Brazil's October presidential election on Saturday, seeking to follow in the footsteps of his father, Jair Bolsonaro.
Far-right firebrand Jair Bolsonaro anointed his eldest son as his successor after being sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup in response to his defeat by leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil's 2022 election.
The Liberal Party (PL) will officially name Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, as its candidate at a convention in Sao Paulo, with Argentina's libertarian President Javier Milei as a guest of honour.
Flavio is promising change: he wants to "free" Brazil from crime, inflation, high taxes and Lula, who is seeking a fourth term in office.
"We are on a plane without a pilot," he said last week.
The senator was neck-and-neck with Lula in the polls until he was hit by a series of scandals, including ties to a disgraced banker, a family feud and new tariffs from ally US President Donald Trump.
Pollster Datafolha published a survey on Friday showing that in a runoff election, Lula would win 48 per cent of votes to Flavio's 43 per cent.
"It is a moment of weakening for Flavio... there is uncertainty over the viability of his candidacy because rejection of him has increased," Marco Teixeira, a political science professor at the Getulio Vargas Foundation, told AFP.
A WAVE OF SCANDALS
Flavio's troubles began in May when an audio recording emerged of him asking banker Daniel Vorcaro — accused in a multi-million-dollar fraud case — to finance a film about his father.
Flavio had denied any contact with Vorcaro and, just hours before the recording was published, told a reporter that the accusation was "a lie". He now maintains their relationship was limited to the film.
On Thursday, a Supreme Court justice ordered an investigation into the financing of the film.
A second crisis hit Flavio's campaign when his stepmother, Michelle Bolsonaro, posted an Instagram video saying he had "disrespected me and mistreated me... he said I didn't understand anything about politics".
The former first lady is key to the right-wing movement's appeal among Brazil's large female and evangelical electorate.
With divisions growing, Flavio read out a letter on social media from Jair Bolsonaro urging unity — contravening the terms of his father's house arrest.
A Supreme Court justice then blocked Flavio from visiting his father until after the first round of voting.
In a bid to unite the right before the convention, Flavio posted a video this week apologising to Michelle, who quickly accepted the gesture of reconciliation.
Flavio Bolsonaro has cast himself as a more moderate version of his father, but is a hardliner on crime and this week echoed his father in raising debunked concerns about Brazil's electronic voting system.
The senator has struggled to seal alliances with Brazil's influential centrist bloc, with key parties announcing they will remain neutral in the October 4 election.
TARIFF TROUBLES
Flavio Bolsonaro has also faced backlash after US President Donald Trump's administration imposed two new sets of tariffs on Brazil this month.
The Bolsonaro family last year backed tariffs on Brazil introduced in retaliation for the trial against the former president, an ally of Trump.
These duties were partly reversed after talks between Brasilia and Washington.
Flavio Bolsonaro unsuccessfully urged the Trump administration to "postpone" new tariffs until after the election so as not to hand Lula a "political victory".
Lula has made tensions with the United States a central campaign issue and has accused his rival of being a "traitor" and putting political interests above economic interests.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six detained in ketum processing operation across Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU: Six men were detained for their involvement in ketum processing and drug-related activities, with equipment and contraband worth more than RM50,000 seized.
The six were arrested during a three-day integrated operation across Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan, which ended on Thursday.
General Operations Force (GOF) Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the operation, codenamed Op Bersepadu MITRA 1/26, began on July 21.
He said the operation was carried out in collaboration with the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) of Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan.
"The operation involved five officers and 53 personnel, who simultaneously raided nine locations identified through intelligence gathering," he added.
Ahmad Radzi said the six suspects, aged between 23 and 44, were arrested at various locations in Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan, with two of them testing positive for methamphetamine.
He said the operation led to the seizure of 274kg of ketum leaves, 986.8 litres of ketum juice, eight plastic drums, four gas cylinders, three cooking pots, three stove sets, three motorcycles, two metal hooks and a ladder.
"The total value of the seizure is estimated at RM55,500.
"All suspects and the seized items have been handed over to the NCID in the respective districts for further investigation and prosecution," he said.
The cases are being investigated under Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952 and Section 15(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC probes Facebook post allegedly insulting Islam
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is investigating a complaint over Facebook content touching on race, religion and royalty (3R) that allegedly insulted Islam.
In a statement today, MCMC said it would not compromise on any misuse of communication platforms that violates the law.
The commission said it was working closely with the police and stood ready to provide technical assistance and digital forensic expertise to support the probe.
The case is being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, which carries a fine of up to RM500,000, a maximum two-year jail term, or both, upon conviction.
MCMC said the dissemination of such content was viewed seriously as it could incite hatred, undermine social unity and threaten national harmony.
It also reminded the public to use social media platforms responsibly and refrain from sharing content that is grossly offensive, insulting or inflammatory, particularly on religious matters.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MINDEF: LIMA'27, DSA & NATSEC Asia 2028 gain global industry backing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition 2027 (LIMA'27), as well as the Defence Services Asia (DSA) and National Security (NATSEC) Asia 2028 exhibitions, have received early commitments from several leading global defence industry players to participate in the events.
Among the companies that have confirmed their participation are Pilatus Aircraft Ltd, RUAG, Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI), Glenair, Team Defence Australia and Kallman Worldwide, while NAICO Malaysia has confirmed its role as a strategic partner.
The Ministry of Defence (MINDEF), in a statement, said the early commitments reflected growing confidence among global defence and aerospace industry players in Malaysia's capability to host international-standard defence exhibitions.
"The development further strengthens LIMA'27 and DSA & NATSEC Asia 2028 as leading international platforms for the defence, aerospace and security sectors, while creating opportunities for strategic cooperation and supporting the growth of the defence industry," it said.
The participation contract signing ceremony involving the international defence companies was held at the Malaysia Pavilion during the Farnborough International Airshow 2026 (FIA 2026) in the United Kingdom.
The ceremony was witnessed by Defence Ministry secretary-general Datuk Lokman Hakim Ali and Air Force chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris.
Mindef said Malaysia's participation in FIA 2026 was expected to boost international participation and further enhance the profile of LIMA'27 and DSA & NATSEC Asia 2028, while opening up opportunities for strategic investments, industry collaboration and technology transfer to support the country's defence industry ecosystem.
It said both exhibitions would continue to serve as strategic platforms for Malaysia's defence diplomacy by strengthening bilateral and multilateral ties with international partners.
"Through these platforms, Malaysia will expand strategic dialogue, facilitate capability development, encourage industry collaboration and strengthen trust and understanding among defence partners.
"This approach is in line with the aspirations of the Sixth Thrust of the National Defence Strategic Plan (PSPN) to strengthen international relations and empower the country's defence industry ecosystem," it said.
LIMA'27 will be held from April 17 to 20, 2027 in Langkawi, jointly organised by Global Exhibition & Conference Sdn Bhd, while DSA & NATSEC Asia 2028 will take place from April 17 to 20, 2028 in Kuala Lumpur, with DSA Exhibition & Conference Sdn Bhd as co-organiser.
– BERNAMA

Title: Six killed in crash on Jalan Karak Lama [WATCH]
Article:
BENTONG: Six men aged between 15 and 25 were killed after the car they were travelling in collided with a one-tonne lorry on Jalan Karak Lama towards Temerloh, near Klinik Desa Jambu Rias, early today.
The victims were pronounced dead at the scene after they were trapped in the car following the crash, which occurred around 4.20am.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Mohd Razam Taja Rahim said the department's operations centre received an emergency call at 4.24am, prompting a team from the Karak Fire and Rescue Station to rush to the scene.
He said the first fire engine arrived at 4.32am and found the crash involving a Toyota Camry and a one-tonne lorry.
"Six male victims in the Toyota Camry were found trapped in the vehicle and were pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry personnel," he said in a statement today.
The deceased were identified as Mugilan Vraputiran, 25; Dinesvaran Kumar, 21; Alaganathan Krishnan, 20; Kanabati Raja Arunasalam, 18; Kiisyen Sasi Kumar, 16; and Paranthaman Marutayah, 15.
[[nid:1496687]]
The lorry driver, Muhamad Hanafi Ahmad Raju, 31, was injured and taken to hospital by a Health Ministry ambulance for further treatment.
Firefighters provided first aid and used specialised rescue equipment, including a Rescue Tool and Combi Tool, to extricate the victims.
"The bodies were handed over to the police for further action, while the injured victim was handed over to Health Ministry personnel," he said.
